title: Hotpath escalation: SLO miss investigation and hotfix validation (ACME)
content:
SUMMARY:
On 2025-08-14 16:23 UTC we observed sustained p99 latency violations for the low-latency hosted inference tier (SLO: p99 <= 200ms). The window of elevated tail latency lasted ~20 minutes with the worst p99 measured at ~440ms. Several committed customers received error escalations (notably ACME Corp) which triggered a customer-facing incident. This doc captures the investigation, profiling artifacts, root cause hypothesis, hotfix steps, validation results, and action items.

INCIDENT TIMELINE (local times shown as UTC):
- 2025-08-14 16:18: rate alarms started to spike (automated alert p99 > 200ms).
- 16:23: Pager duty escalated to on-call SRE and runtime team.
- 16:27: Devs confirm p99 ~ 350-440ms across multiple clusters; error rates low but timeouts increased slightly.
- 16:32: Customer success (CS) notified ACME account team; ACME opened an escalation (RT-1327).
- 16:40: Initial mitigation: roll back of a recent kernel-selection heuristic (PR 3456) on a small canary pool.
- 16:56: Canary nodes show p99 recovery to ~180ms; full rollback initiated.
- 17:15: Full rollback completed across affected pools. Metrics returned to baseline by 17:30.

IMPACT:
- SLO miss window: ~16:20 - 17:30 UTC (peak between 16:23 - 16:45).
- Customers impacted: ACME Corp (reported via escalation), subset of hosted low-latency customers routed to affected regions (us-west2).
- Business impact: elevated latency causing degraded UX; no confirmed data loss.

INITIAL HYPOTHESES CONSIDERED:
1) Autoscaling thrash leading to cold nodes and KV cache misses.
2) Network flakiness between control plane and GPUs (host-to-device transfers).
3) New kernel-selection heuristic (PR 3456) causing unexpected kernel path which increased host-mediated transfers and disabled a micro-cache fastpath.
4) Sudden workload distribution shift (large-batch spam) causing queueing.

DIAGNOSTICS AND PROFILING STEPS TAKEN:
- Collected runtime traces (per-request trace ids) for 10k sampled requests in the window (trace archive id: trc-20250814-16).
- Captured flamegraphs from CPU (perf record) and GPU (nsys snapshots) on canary nodes.
- Enabled debug-level kv-cache metrics: hit_rate, eviction_rate, prefix_match_miss.
- Examined kernel selection logs (runtime DEBUG logging) where the heuristic picks whether to use fused-kernel vs fallback.
- Replayed representative request traces in a dedicated staging harness (replay run id: replay-0825-hotpath).

KEY FINDINGS:
- KV cache eviction rate spiked ~7x during the incident window on affected nodes. prefix_match_miss increased from 0.8% baseline to 12.4%.
- Flamegraphs showed increased time in host-side serialization and memcpy paths (cpu: copy_to_device, cudaMemcpyAsync overhead).
- nsys GPU snapshots: kernel occupancy unchanged, but there was a 2x increase in small host->device memcpy operations (many tiny transfers instead of a single batched transfer).
- Kernel-selection heuristic (PR 3456) had a regression for short sequence lengths: it preferred a memory-layout that bypassed the pre-allocated KV fastpath for sequences <= 64 tokens when certain alignment conditions were met. This caused per-token small memcpy calls and frequent kv-cache entry churn.
- Replay of production traces in staging reproduced the tail latency uplift when the PR 3456 logic was enabled. Reverting the heuristic restored baseline p99.

NUMBERS (representative):
- Baseline (pre-incident): p50=28ms, p95=90ms, p99=160ms, p999=265ms.
- Incident peak: p50=35ms, p95=120ms, p99=440ms, p999=820ms.
- Post-rollback: p50=30ms, p95=92ms, p99=170ms.
- KV cache: hit_rate baseline 94.2% -> during incident 81.0%; eviction_rate baseline 0.3/s -> 2.1/s.

ROOT CAUSE (concise):
A regression introduced by a kernel-selection and memory-layout heuristic (PR 3456) caused the runtime to bypass a pre-allocated KV cache fastpath for many short sequences. That bypass produced many small host->device memory copies and frequent KV cache churn, increasing CPU-side serialization and tail latency. The heuristic worked on average but had a corner-case alignment bug that affected a sizable fraction of incoming short-sequence requests routed to us-west2.

MITIGATION & HOTFIX:
- Immediate: Reverted PR 3456 in the runtime on canary nodes (rollback initiated 16:40).
- Progressive rollout of rollback across all affected pools (16:56 - 17:15).
- Customer communication: CS sent an initial incident message to ACME at 16:45, followed by status updates at 17:20 and a formal incident summary later.
- Hotfix (short term): create a guarded patch that ensures the KV fastpath is used for sequences <= 128 unless explicit memory constraints are present (PR 3462).
- Long term: add unit tests and fuzz tests for kernel-selection heuristic; add a runtime guard that rejects micro-copy paths if estimated host-copy ops > threshold.

HOTFIX VALIDATION (procedures and results):
1) Local microbenchmarks: executed token-generation microbench with short sequences (len 8-64) using both layouts; measured memcpy counts and latency. Result: guarded patch reduced memcpy ops by ~75% and p99 by 60% in microbench.
2) Staging replay: used the production trace archive (trc-20250814-16) and replayed across identical staging pool sizes. Result: enabling guarded patch matched baseline p99 within +-15ms across 10 runs.
3) Canary rollout: deployed guarded patch to a 5% canary pool for 30 minutes while monitoring SLOs and KV metrics. Result: canary p99 stable at ~170ms; no increase in eviction_rate.
4) Production roll-forward: full deployment after 90 minutes of stable canary metrics. Monitored for 2 hours with no regression observed.

VALIDATION METRICS (text summary):
- memcpy_op_count_per_request: baseline 1.8 -> incident 6.7 -> post-hotfix 2.1
- kv_cache_hit_rate: baseline 94.2% -> incident 81.0% -> post-hotfix 93.6%
- p99 latency: baseline 160ms -> incident 440ms -> post-hotfix 170ms

CUSTOMER ESCALATION NOTES (ACME):
- ACME reported a perceivable slowdown for their inference flows at 16:28. CS escalated to eng at 16:30.
- Engineering provided a rolling status at 16:45 and 17:20.
- A post-incident technical write-up and replay artifacts were shared with ACME on 2025-08-15 EOD.
- ACME requested guarantees about recurrence prevention; we committed to the test and guard additions below and offered a 3-month performance monitoring report.

POST-INCIDENT ACTIONS (owners + ETA):
- (Priya) Add unit + fuzz tests for kernel-selection heuristic and land by 2025-08-22.
- (Eric) Add a runtime micro-metrics export for memcpy_op_count and per-request kv-cache decisions (Prometheus) by 2025-08-20.
- (Diego) Implement a runtime threshold guard that forces fastpath use when potential host-copy ops > X and land a safe toggle by 2025-09-01.
- (Maya) Coordinate customer followups and shared replay artifacts with ACME and other impacted customers by 2025-08-16.
- (SRE) Add an automated alert for sudden kv_cache_eviction_rate > 1.0/s by 2025-08-18.

OPEN QUESTIONS / NOTES:
- Why did the regression disproportionately affect us-west2? Early theory: traffic mix there has more short-chat workloads with specific alignment patterns; we need per-region sampling to confirm.
- Could the kernel heuristic changes have been covered by existing unit tests? Tests missed layout alignment permutations.
- Consider instrumenting the compiler/optimizer outputs to tag paths that transition off-fastpath for easier triage.

RELATED ARTIFACTS / REFERENCES:
- Jira: RT-1327 (customer escalation)
- PRs: 3456 (regression), 3462 (guarded patch), follow-up PRs for tests.
- Replays: replay-0825-hotpath, trace archive trc-20250814-16.
- Slack: incident thread #runtime-hotpath-2025-08-14.

APPENDIX (diagnostic commands and snippets):
- Perf flamegraph capture (canary node):
  sudo perf record -F 99 -g -p `pidof runtime_process` -- sleep 30
  sudo perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl | ./flamegraph.pl > perf-0825-canary.svg

- nsys capture:
  nsys profile -o nsys-0825-canary --sample=none --trace=cuda,cudnn --capture-range c -p `pidof runtime_process`

- Quick grep from runtime logs: kernel-selection entries
  2025-08-14T16:22:45Z [DEBUG] kernel-select: seq_len=24 align=48 pref_fastpath=false reason=align_mismatch path=fallback

- Replay harness command (staging):
  ./replay --trace trc-20250814-16 --parallelism 32 --routes us-west2 --output replay-0825-hotpath/results.json

CONCLUSION:
We identified and rolled back a kernel-selection heuristic regression that increased small host->device memory operations and bypassed the KV cache fastpath for many short-sequence requests. The guarded hotfix restores baseline behavior; additional testing, metrics, and a runtime guard will be added to prevent regression recurrence.

NOTES TO SELF (rough):
- Add checklist for kernel-selection PRs: include microbench targets for p99 with short sequences + explicit check for memcpy_op_count.
- Consider a "fastpath-safety" CI job that runs on PRs touching kernel selection.
